name: Least privilege across every IAM role, and how we would know: a posture number carrying its denominator and vintage, per-role unused-permission visibility at PERMISSION grain, the condition axis a policy requires, declared-vs-live role reconciliation with a separate governance disposition, pre-flight blast radius before any narrowing, and an assessment that can be re-run.
description: Commissioned when Andrew asked whether NFRA_OPSEC202609 covered IAM least privilege; the measured answer was NO (brief F1), which produced a project rather than an amendment. Eight ratified outcomes. The central problem is stated by the brief itself (F4): the estate's tooling is pointed at what a role MAY do and cannot answer what it DOES, and least privilege is a question about the gap. Ruling 20 settles instrument direction as EXTEND comp-iam-usage to permission grain -- it is BUILT, tracked and self-testing -- with AWS Access Analyzer as a fallback whose per-role price nobody has read. The 16 undeclared roles of 208 are a SETTLED SET, not just a settled count, and they carry TWO remedies that do not move together: governance (should this be in code at all) and permissions (is it over-granted).

blocking: No L5/L6 SEAT. The PRD is complete and decomposable; there is no COO lane on this project. FOUR CARRIED FACTS THE DECOMPOSITION MUST NOT LOSE: (1) C-EXTEND-NOT-BUILD -- comp-iam-usage is BUILT, tracked, executable and self-test passing (brief F5 CORRECTED); a cell written as greenfield re-buys working code, and this seat made exactly that error earlier in the session by calling the instrument the hardest problem when a third of it already existed. (2) C-TWO-REMEDIES -- the 16 undeclared roles need a GOVERNANCE disposition and a PERMISSIONS disposition, they do not move together, and manifest rows S5 and S6 are separate BY CONTRACT for that reason. (3) FWD-5's bar is EXERCISED and must not be softened to APPLIED: a pre-flight check never run against a real narrowing is indistinguishable from one that always answers 'nothing breaks', and the failure it prevents is an outage this project would cause itself. (4) C-ANALYZER-PRICED-FIRST -- AWS Access Analyzer is the FALLBACK and NO PER-ROLE PRICE HAS BEEN READ BY ANYONE; taking it off the shelf is a VENDOR call requiring Andrew's explicit word, never an assumption inherited from the brief.
